_comment: Single manifest for the one-skill builder. Everything the merged skill contains is
declared here: which upstream repos feed it, which files each contributes, and which
1. add an entry to "sources" with an "origin" (github repo + the glob list to vendor)
2. add skill entries to that source's "skills" list, each with a bucket + when + entry
3. run:  python one-skill/build.py sync && python one-skill/build.py all
Nothing else in the repository needs to change; SKILL.md, the router table, the
provenance block and the install copies are all regenerated from this file.

skill.name: one-skill
skill.title: One Skill — grug · caveman · documents · antislop · pocock · anthropic
skill.tagline: Everything in this repository, in one skill: how to think, how much to write, how it reads, how the interface looks, and how the work moves from idea to merged.
skill.description: One skill for any coding, writing, review, design or planning task: grug's reasoning, caveman's compression, a professional document register, the antislop design filter, Pocock's process, Anthropic's engineering and skill-authoring workflows. Triggers: "one skill", "caveman", "be brief", "ringkas", "antislop". Register by destination, code byte-exact, one reference at a time.
skill.allowed_tools: Read Write Edit Glob Grep Bash(python3 *)

not_vendored.what: bin/ (472 KB), renderers/ (1.6 MB), schemas/ (72 KB), assets/ (720 KB), examples/ (4 MB), test/ (3.7 MB)
not_vendored.reason: The `bin/` (472 KB), `renderers/` (1.6 MB), `schemas/` (72 KB), `assets/` (720 KB) and `examples/` (4 MB) are a Node 18 pipeline with npm deps. A skill cannot install them, and a diagram 'validated' by a renderer that is not present would be a fabricated artifact. Only the authoring judgement that survives without the tool is carried.

Every one of them is a contract with the renderer: layout rules expressed as schema fields, delivery gates defined as CLI commands, and the repair procedure that ends in `finalize` and `visual-check`. Carrying them would put instructions in the bundle for commands that are not in the bundle, which is the failure mode this whole merge is built to avoid.

sources.license: see the pack (LICENSE.txt inside the skill directory)

origin.note: Vendored from the archive committed to this repository on 2026-10-10, pinned by sha256. The pack's own skill name is `skill-creator-copy` — that is the directory the text came from, which is why the inventory matches that name. This closes the gap the handoff used to list as open: the repository had no meta-skill for writing skills.

not_vendored.what: scripts/ (run_eval.py, aggregate_benchmark.py, improve_description.py, package_skill.py, quick_validate.py, run_loop.py), agents/ (grader, comparator, analyzer), eval-viewer/, assets/eval_review.html, references/schemas.md
not_vendored.reason: The evaluation half of the pack. It spawns `claude` subprocesses with and without the skill, grades assertions, serves an HTML viewer, and optimises the frontmatter description by variance — all of which need the CLI, an API key, subagents and a browser. The two validators additionally import PyYAML, which this repository deliberately does not depend on: `build.py check` is the local equivalent of `quick_validate.py`. The authoring judgement survives; the harness that measures it does not. Instructions to run a harness this bundle cannot invoke are exactly what the implementability filter exists to stop.

skills.title: Authoring a skill — intent, progressive disclosure, writing style
skills.when: the user asks to write, restructure, review or generalise a skill, or asks why a skill is shaped the way it is
skills.strip_reason: Drafting test prompts is worth reading; running them is the eval harness (subagents, the `claude` CLI, a browser viewer) this bundle does not carry.
skills.note: The craft half of skill-creator, kept while its measurement half is dropped. It says what this repository's build says from the other direction: always-on judgement in `SKILL.md`, depth in reference files that say when to read them, explain why instead of stacking MUSTs, and generalise rather than overfit to the examples in front of you.
